     2	If you craft an immediate effect, resolve it and discard 
     3	the card. Often these effects will let you take an item 
     4	from the supply on the map and score victory points. 
     5	If the item supply on the map does not have the listed 
     6	item to take, you cannot craft the card.
     7	If you craft a persistent effect, place the card in your 
     8	play area. You may use its effect. You cannot craft a per­
     9	sistent effect if you have one of the same name.
    10	Move (4.2)
    11	Take any of your warriors and pawns from one clearing 
    12	and move them along a linking path to one adjacent 
    13	clearing.
    14	You must rule the origin, destination, or both. A given 
    15	piece can be moved any number of times per turn.
    16	Battle (4.3)
    17	You can battle in a clearing with your warriors or pawn.
    18	Step 1: Defender May Ambush. Attacker may cancel 
    19	defender’s ambush card by also playing ambush card.
    20	Step 2: Use Before-Roll Effects. Players may use op­
    21	tional battle effects that say “before the roll.”
    22	Step 3: Roll Dice. Attacker will deal hits equal to higher 
    23	roll. Defender will deal hits equal to lower roll. 
    24	The maximum hits you can deal by rolling equals your 
    25	number of warriors in the clearing of battle. 
    26	Step 4: Use After-Roll Effects. Players may use optional 
    27	battle effects that do not say “before the roll.”
    28	Step 5: Count Hits. Players count up the total number 
    29	of hits they deal. Some effects deal extra hits, which 
    30	are not limited by warriors. Some effects ignore hits, 
    31	subtracting them.
    32	Defenseless: If the defender has no warriors in the clear­
    33	ing of battle, the attacker deals an extra hit.
    34	Step 6: Deal Hits. Each hit removes one piece—
    35	warriors first, then buildings and tokens, as chosen by 
    36	the player taking the hits.
    37	Remember: Score a victory point each time 
    38	you remove an enemy building or token.
